Short $PZZA: Shaq excitement wearing off
Two weeks ago this was posted: [https://www.reddit.com/r/wallstreetbets/comments/b48mbb/](https://www.reddit.com/r/wallstreetbets/comments/b48mbb/shaq_joining_board_of_directors_of_pzza_get_ready/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web2x)

WSB was right, and $PZZA did have a good spike after the news, going from $47 up past $53 at the end of last week. This week, they've been back on their usual downtrend, falling to $52.10 at close Friday, having touched as low as $50.50 Thursday afternoon. $PZZA's been on a general disappointing downtrend in the last year, and it's likely to continue. I take last week's sink in prices as indication that the spike was indeed excitement about Shaq, and that as it wears off the price should settle back down to where it was, around $50 or lower.

My position: I opened a short when the Shaq spike happened on the 22nd, but pulled the plug two days later when it became clear the surge wasn't over yet. Been waiting to see when/where the price would top, and I think last Friday was the tippy top. I'm considering opening another short position in $PZZA next week, depending on conditions Monday morning.

All it takes is a small move for a far-out option to be not quite so far-out (and thus worth more; profit for you). If you buy a far-out put *and* a far-out call on a security, one of them must gain when the underlying moves in its direction. (If you are playing this spread, the other option contract will probably become worth $0, so you're counting on a move to at least three cents to become truly profitable.) Remember: if it goes from 1 cent up to 2 cents, that's double your money. If it goes from 4 cents to 6 cents, that's still a 50% profit.

If the underlying price is sure to move sufficiently and is equally likely to go in either direction, a one-cent option has a 50% chance of (at least) doubling in value.

Note that this is advice on having fun with FDs, and not serious investment advice. "Move sufficiently" is the magic term above which depends on market pricing; judging it involves looking at historical volatility and judging whether the premium is underpriced, and other dweeby bullshit. Theta can steal your lunch on both sides if the underlying doesn't move enough.

items.title: WSB PSA: Option premiums crazy high? Consider *selling* FDs instead.
items.text:
WSB PSA: Option premiums crazy high? Consider *selling* FDs instead.
I'm fairly new to options trading, and I know a lot of you are similar. I'm here to share a good position I opened on Monday (keep your fingers crossed for me it doesn't go tits up, cuz she ain't over yet), and lay some learnin' on y'all.

I had a hunch that NFLX was going to go up after their ER tonight, so I wanted to buy some calls. I opened up the 4/18 option chain and was shocked. "300% time value?? Ain't no way I'm paying that." So instead of just leaving my great hunch behind, I took advantage of those high premiums: I sold puts.

**The Bull Put Spread**

A bull put spread is when you sell a put and also buy a lower-strike put to cap your losses.

Monday morning at open, a NFLX 352.5 put was trading for nearly $15 a share (so $1500 a contract). My broker wisely required I commit nearly $10k of my margin to sell that put, and I didn't feel like closing other positions to enter a new one. What to do? Buy a way-OTM put for $30. 😎This took the margin impact down to \~$3K, since my losses were now capped at $6,750 rather than $35,250. Not bad for thirty bucks.

I sold a 352.5/285 put spread for $1400 in total (14.30 for the 352.5 put, 0.30 for the 285 put). 

**Lessons**

* *When premiums are high, profit from others' FOMO by writing options.* Short options won't ever blow up like everyone's DIS calls did last week, but think of how much loss porn from options is on this sub. You know who keeps all that money? Options sellers.
* *Theta always makes money.* Stonks go up and stonks go down, but time always goes forward. Theta is constantly making you money; all you have to do is make sure that profit isn't offset too badly by a move in the underlying. Case in point: when NFLX dipped like 5% when the ER came out today, *I was still up $200*. (The high premium made sure of that)

SELL OPTIONS  
ITS FREE MONEY!!
